subject: Media Literacy
title: Satire Mistaken for News
description: A fast breakdown of Satire Mistaken for News for builders.

hook.text: The Onion published a fake story about a Congressman. A news outlet reported it as real. The cycle begins.

buildup.text: Satire — intentionally humorous fiction — is often shared out of context and mistaken for genuine news.

discovery.text: Social media strips context. A satirical headline shared without the source looks identical to real news.

twist.text: Some disinformation creators deliberately disguise false content as satire to avoid accountability.

climax.text: In a world where satire and reality are equally absurd, telling them apart requires active verification.

punchline.text: When reality is stranger than satire, confusion isn't surprising.

quiz.question: Why is satire frequently mistaken for real news?
options: Social media strips context, making satirical headlines look like real news
People don't have a sense of humor
